These auditors typically learn from a limited corpus of trajectories with verified outcomes. Expanding this corpus requires costly execution and verification, yet broader failure coverage alone provides no explicit criterion for identifying prefixes that the current auditor finds difficult to classify. items.summary: AI agents increasingly use files and software tools to produce professional deliverables. Such work draws on materials, decisions, and feedback accumulated across assignments. We introduce OfficeTown, a generative simulation framework for professional organizations in which tasks and their context arise from continuing organizational work. Evaluating scientific judgment is difficult because research decisions are open-ended and depend on project context. We construct SciΠvot, a 248-case benchmark of scientific judgment based on human corrections. items.title: MorphAct: Robot Policies Morphing with the Worlds They Act In
items.summary: Progress toward general intelligence in the physical world requires scaling robot learning across diverse environments and interactions. However, existing robot policies use shared parameters that remain fixed across interaction contexts. When different operations favor competing parameter adjustments, fitting their mixture can leave individual operations insufficiently adapted. items.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) commonly couple video and action experts through dense, layer-wise Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) attention, exposing action prediction to irrelevant visual features while enforcing matched expert depths. This coupling hinders selective visual-feature use and introduces redundant computation. We introduce Bridge-of-Experts (BoE), instantiated as BridgeWAM, which aggregates visual, language, and proprioceptive priors through 32 Latent Bridge Queries (LBQs) into a shared, limited latent space. items.summary: Retrieval is a fundamental task in multimodal systems: given an image or text query, the goal is to find the most relevant images or texts in a collection, often using a shared embedding space. items.summary: Peer review is under strain from the growth of submissions, and review comments written by humans or AI can misstate what a paper says. We introduce ReviewFact, a benchmark that labels such factual errors in review comments under one definition across NLP, machine learning, and the natural sciences, and that measures cost and latency alongside accuracy. items.summary: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) receive image-generation supervision that exposes them to visual information not fully documented in text. Can learning to generate images expand what pretrained models know? We introduce Knowledge Transfer Probing (KTP), a controlled protocol that supplies new knowledge through image-generation training and tests its accessibility through text-only question answering. items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) progressively revise their predictions across Transformer layers, yet we typically observe only the final output, discarding the trajectory through which it is formed. We introduce Belief-Trajectory Energy(BTE), a model-grounded measure that characterizes an input through the layerwise predictive revisions it induces in a model. items.summary: A coding agent works on repositories that can be far larger than its context window can hold. Prompt compressors and retrievers offer solutions to this problem, but patching an issue needs two things at once: the files that must change, and their code exactly as written, since the model must reproduce the lines it edits. Retrievers rank code by its similarity to the issue rather than by whether it must change, and compressors delete text to fit the budget. items.summary: As joint audio-video generation models become more capable, they can generate audio-visual scenes exhibiting three forms of complexity: multi-event composition, multi-layer audio mixture, and asymmetric cross-modal relations. However, current evaluations largely reuse metrics from earlier simple and unidirectional tasks. They typically evaluate an audio-video clip as a whole and rely on simple predefined relations, making them unsuitable for these increasingly complex scenes. items.title: LEV: Thinking Fast and Deep with Looped Decision Models
items.summary: Decision models answer typed questions about an input with one probability per option, computed in a single forward pass without generating text. Like the fast System 1 of dual-process theory, they answer at once, but their depth is fixed at training time, so they spend the same computation on easy and hard questions. Models that reason in generated text can think longer, but they pay for every extra step in decoded tokens. items.title: Resisting Harmful Instructions through Training-Free Weight Editing
items.summary: Instruction-following language models can comply with requests that conflict with intended behaviors and safety alignment. We introduce a training-free weight-editing approach for reducing compliance with targeted undesirable instructions. Our method needs only forward passes on a small set of prompt pairs per target behavior, and because the edit is stored in the model's weights, changing or deleting instructions in the prompt cannot undo the weight modification. items.summary: Looped language models reuse physical Transformer blocks across logical depth, but established architectures entangle recurrence placement, input injection, and recurrent state organization. We isolate these axes in models trained from scratch at matched parameter scale, logical depth, and token budgets, and then test whether the resulting design principles transfer to resident- and active-parameter-matched Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. items.title: DAGFormer: Global Topology Prediction for Transformer Cross-Layer Connections
items.summary: We propose DAGFormer, a Transformer language model whose cross-layer connections are planned by a jointly trained topology predictor. Beyond the residual connections in a standard Transformer, DAGFormer adds direct connections from earlier layers to later ones, and the predictor controls the strength of every connection based on input tokens. items.summary: Self-evolving language models train on tasks they generate, so every round must decide which updated model the next round inherits. Current loops such as R-Zero, Agent0, and Skill Self-Play make this decision through the task, admitting tasks that look learnable and inheriting every resulting update. items.summary: Recent closed-source image generation systems can produce diverse visual content from simple compositions to information-dense graphics, yet open-weight text-to-image models still struggle with dense text and intricate layouts. To narrow this gap, we introduce MOSS-Image, an open generation system that combines high-fidelity visual synthesis with intent-aware composition. items.summary: Dynamic Gaussian representations have made high-quality, real-time volumetric video increasingly practical, yet challenging motion can still break their reconstruction: small fast-moving objects may disappear, and fine textures in highly dynamic regions are often lost. In particular, simply training longer or using more Gaussians may still fail to recover small, fast-moving objects. items.title: Execution Before Memory: Diagnosing Memory Failures in Video World Models
items.summary: A memory test for a video world model should say whether the scene was set, whether the asked change was carried out, and whether the last frame shows the result. Current tests fold these into one number, so a low score is easy to read as forgetting. When the change is not carried out, the hidden state transition cannot appear, so the test is not really a test of memory. items.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
items.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. Hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting. items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) hold broad knowledge in one set of weights, but lack interpretability and trustworthy reasoning, especially in high-stakes use cases. items.summary: Transcribing expressive piano performances into scores requires interpreting individual note timings within an underlying metrical structure. However, score attributes are associated with notes, whereas beats may occur without coincident note onsets. items.summary: Generated videos often lose geometric consistency under camera motion: structures warp under viewpoint change, parallax becomes inconsistent, and smooth camera movement may collapse into shot-like transitions. We argue that this failure is largely a data problem. In web-scale video corpora, most visible motion comes from dynamic objects captured by static or weakly moving cameras, leaving only sparse supervision for viewpoint-induced appearance changes. items.summary: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) can induce behaviors beyond those explicitly targeted. For example, training a model to respond more warmly can make it more sycophantic, and training it to write insecure code can cause broad misalignment on prompts unrelated to coding. items.summary: Reproducible and analytically robust research findings are essential to scientific progress, but evaluating these properties typically requires costly manual effort. We investigate whether LLM agents can help automate reproduction and robustness analysis, using a medical case study grounded in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, a widely used U.S. cancer registry underlying tens of thousands of published studies. items.summary: Pretrained VLMs bring rich world knowledge and semantic priors to object-goal navigation, and fine-tuning a VLM into a navigation policy has become a common recipe. items.summary: Scientific discovery requires developing worthwhile hypotheses into practical investigations, yet learning from this evolving research process remains challenging. We introduce an operational definition of valuable and testable research hypotheses: evidence-grounded claims about consequential uncertainties, coupled with feasible investigations, explicit decision criteria, and alternative explanations. items.summary: Parameterized quantum circuits are widely investigated in quantum machine learning, yet how their architecture can provide task-aligned inductive biases remains poorly understood. items.summary: A reasoning trace can accompany a correct answer without providing effective supervision for a particular student. items.summary: 10月15日，可灵AI新一代视频生成模型 Kling 4.0 正式上线。 真实、可控、专业，是这一代模型升级的核心方向。Kling 4.0 聚焦高动态、强运镜的视频创作场景，在三个方向实现集中突破：大幅度动态表现更稳定，提升高速运动与复杂运镜的连贯性；单次原生生成最长可达30秒，支持长镜头与连续叙事，导演思维全程在线；全能参考支持最多15项参考素材组合，同时支持最多10张关键帧输入，帮助创作者将一个构思转化为完整作品。 与专业创作者建立深度链接，与其共同完成作品创作，尤其是核心镜头的高质量交付，是可灵模型持续迭代的重要方向。 专业创作者需要的不只是偶然生成惊艳画面，更要稳定完成决定作品品质的关键镜头，并让生成素材进入完整制作流程。可灵AI相信，技术的价值，不只是让内容得以生成，更是让每一帧画面背后的‘用心’能被看见。无论是承载情绪的特写，还是决定整部作品质感的关键画面，每一个倾注心血的镜头，都值得被认真呈现。 能“文”更能“武”，大幅动态与复杂运镜更“稳” 一直以来，可灵AI的“文戏”凭借对人物情感细腻生动的演绎，堪称影视工业级水准。在此基础上，Kling 4.0 重点攻克了AI视频的高频痛点，大幅度动态与复杂运镜表现更加稳定流畅：无论是高速运动、连续动作，还是跟拍、环绕等大幅镜头运动，都能保持画面稳定、过程连贯，再激烈的大场面也能从容驾驭，让AI视频生成真正迈向“生产级交付”。 …

今天开车被迫窝囊了一次
items.summary: 开车等红灯，还剩三四十秒时，前车往前跑了一段，空了大概十几米距离。我没动，准备快变灯时再起步过去。 这时候后面车开始滴滴滴打喇叭，我想着反正红灯又走不了，就没理他。随后他一个猛拐，从左车道饶过我去前面了，我还是没在意，又走不了，你想塞就塞呗。 此时我前面有两辆车。绿灯亮了，大家正常起步，我跟在后面。这时有意思的事情发生了：前车压上斑马线后，突然一个急刹不动了，过了四五秒，又挪了一下，随后又是一脚刹停。 我一下子明白了，感情这是报复我来了。就这样，他一直卡到黄灯才走。我这时还比较淡定，只是随口骂了句 SB ，心想：这不是给我送证据让我举报吗？装了这么久的海康威视行车记录仪终于要派上用场了。我还特意瞄了眼时间，方便后面找视频。 下车时，我把内存卡拔了下来，带回家，翻出尘封已久的读卡器，连上电脑。然后就傻眼了：这特么什么情况？怎么那个时间段一个视频都没有？要说坏了，但是后面还有新的视频，卡也没满啊？ 不死心，又翻了几遍其它目录，最后确定没有。不过倒是发现了一个规律：这记录仪好像每次只会记录起步和停车的几分钟，中间全是空的？不是哥们，这科学吗？ 这下子尴尬了，本以为能重拳出击呢，没想到小丑竟是我自己，只能窝囊忍着了。 给 V 友们丢脸了 😭

items.title: 发现大家对拖欠工资这件事接受度很高
items.summary: 入职现在的公司已经差不多 4 年，每个月准时发工资，节假日提前发。 这个月突然说资金周转不过来，工资需要拖一下，最快月底会发，实际上去年年终奖金也拖到现在快年底了，也还没发，估计是泡汤了。 但我发现同事们对这件事，基本上就是打趣一两句公司是不是不行了，然后就闭嘴不谈了，每天还是热火朝天的干活，开会，讨论需求，特别积极。 我真有点理解不了他们的动力是从哪里来的，我上班 8 年 从来没遇到过拖欠工资的，明显这公司也快到头了，我看情况再过一两月最多过完年肯定得撤了，目前很摆，什么周报的直接不写。 虽然我也明白这改变不了什么，但只能说还是很不爽吧。

items.title: [送激活码] 我做了一个跟随 Finder 窗口的路径工具 FinderNav，送 80 个激活码
items.summary: 🎉 FinderNav for macOS 开启首轮公开测试！ 大家好，我是 FinderNav 的开发者。 在深层目录里切换祖先目录、返回刚才访问的位置、复制文件路径或在终端中打开当前目录时，Finder 的这些入口比较分散。 所以我做了 **FinderNav** —— 一款原生的 macOS Finder 增强工具。 它不会替代 Finder ，也不会修改 Finder 本身，而是跟随当前 Finder 窗口，在底部增加一条轻量的悬浮导航栏，把路径导航和常用文件操作集中在随手可及的位置。 Finder 自带的路径栏主要用于展示和跳转； FinderNav 在此基础上加入了收藏、最近访问、Quick Access 、路径复制、终端打开和文件操作，并会跟随当前 Finder 窗口。 ![FinderNav 界面预览]( https://static-cjys.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/FInderNav/738e7cd1-3ba8-475e-bc2b-54f8835379b6.png) ### 路径面包屑导航 FinderNav 会显示当前 Finder 窗口所在的完整路径。点击任意一级目录，就能直接跳转，不再需要一层层返回。 ### 收藏与最近访问 常用文件夹可以直接收藏；刚刚访问过的路径也会自动记录，方便快速回到之前的位置。 收藏、历史和设置…
